title: Sourcing & Contracting: Thresholds, Approval Matrix, and RevRec Readiness Checklist
author: Alexandra Park
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines standardized sourcing and contracting thresholds, the approval matrix for commercial commitments, and a step-by-step revenue recognition (RevRec) readiness checklist to ensure clean handoffs between procurement, legal, finance, and sales/GTMS. It is intended for commercial leaders, procurement owners, legal counsel, and finance analysts who manage or review vendor agreements, purchase commitments, and recurring subscription arrangements.

Scope:
- Applies to all third-party vendor commitments (SaaS, professional services, cloud providers, hardware) and customer-facing contracting templates that have financial impact.
- Exempts petty cash purchases (< $2,500) and pre-approved travel/card expenses described in company expense policy.

Goals:
- Reduce RevRec rework and delayed revenue by surfacing recognition constraints at contracting time.
- Ensure consistent approval routing and authority limits.
- Standardize required contracting artifacts and metadata for billing systems.

1) Approval thresholds and routing (summary table)
| Commitment Value (ARR/One-time) | Required Approvals | Procurement Steps | Legal Review | Finance Review |
|----------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------------|----------------|
| <$50K                            | Procurement Lead   | PR + PO           | Standard T&Cs | Optional       |
| $50K - $250K                      | Procurement Manager + Finance Partner | SOW + PO | Legal commercial review (standard clause check) | Finance contract economics review |
| $250K - $1M                       | Procurement Manager + Finance Director + Legal Counsel | Negotiation playbook, Risk assessment | Legal commercial + IP/data clause review | Revenue recognition preliminary assessment |
| > $1M                             | VP Procurement + VP Finance + General Counsel + CEO (if strategic) | Exec sponsor identified; procurement strategy doc required | Full legal review; exec approval required | Contract economics + RevRec pre-commit signoff |

Notes on routing: all approvals must be recorded in the procurement system (Coupa/NetSuite/ProcurePort — whichever is in use) with the ticket/PO number referenced in the contract metadata. If multiple currencies are present, approvals are based on USD equivalent using the corporate FX table at time of request.

2) Quick contracting decision flow (numbered procedure)
1. Requestor creates PR in procurement system with estimated value and selects vendor record.
2. Procurement validates vendor (KYC/sanctions) and confirms vendor onboarding status. If not onboarded, follow supplier onboarding checklist.
3. Procurement assigns preliminary threshold bucket and routes for approvals per table above.
4. Legal receives redline request; legal classifies deviation level: minor (w/in approved playbook), moderate (requires clause exceptions logged), major (exec escalation).
5. Finance runs RevRec preliminary assessment: is there a deliverable schedule, usage-based pricing, significant cancellation rights, or multi-element arrangement?
6. If RevRec flags exist, finance and commercial owner agree on contract language that clarifies billing events and performance obligations.
7. All approvals captured; procurement issues PO or signs contract per delegated authority.
8. Post-signature: procurement uploads executed agreement and metadata to contract repository and notifies Billing/RevRec mailbox.

3) RevRec readiness checklist (to be completed before signature)
- Contract metadata present: counterparty legal name, tax ID/registration, billing address, currency, contract start/end dates, payment terms, PO number (if applicable).
- Commercial model clarification: one-time vs recurring, subscription cadence, seats/units, discounting, prepaid vs billed-in-arrears.
- Performance obligations: clearly documented deliverables and acceptance criteria (for professional services, include milestones and acceptance process).
- Terminations & Refunds: explicit cancellation rights and refund or pro-rate rules.
- Modification/change order process documented: how amendments affect billing and recognition.
- Usage meters/metrics: for usage-based pricing, confirm metric definition, reporting cadence, and invoicing lag.
- Transfer of control: identify when customer obtains benefit (trigger for recognition).
- Contractual billing triggers: invoicing events mapped to performance obligations (e.g., activation, month-end, milestone completion).
- Specific RevRec constraints noted: variable consideration estimates, significant financing component, customer acceptance holdbacks.
- Finance sign-off (name & date) confirming recognition approach and initial GL mapping.

4) Required contracting artifacts and naming conventions
- Executed Agreement PDF attached and indexed as: {COUNTERPARTY_SHORTNAME}_{CONTRACTTYPE}_{YYYYMMDD}_EXEC.pdf
- Purchase Order record: PO-{VENDOR}-{YYYY}-{NNNN}
- SOWs/Work Orders attached and linked with change order history maintained as separate docs.
- Required fields in contract repository metadata (all mandatory): contract_id, vendor_legal_name, vendor_tax_id, start_date, end_date, payment_terms, billing_contact_email, finance_owner, procurement_owner, PO_number.

5) Procurement-to-Billing handoff (checklist)
- Notify billing@redwood with: executed agreement, PO (if applicable), approved pricing schedule, billing contact, and required GL strings.
- Populate billing instruction template (sample below) and include invoice frequency, net terms, and special billing notes.
- Confirm ERP vendor master data is accurate (tax ID, remit-to address, currency).
- For subscription ARR, confirm product-code-to-GL mapping and recognized revenue account with Finance.

Sample billing instruction (to include in email):
- Vendor: <Legal Name>
- Contract ID: <contract_id>
- Billing cadence: Monthly/Quarterly/Annually
- Billing trigger: e.g., Activation Date / Month-end / Milestone X
- Net terms: Net 30/60/90
- Invoice recipient: billing@redwood (with AP contact copied)
- Special instructions: e.g., consolidate multi-invoices into monthly summary, attach usage report.

6) Standard clause guidance (legal highlights)
- Data residency & security: require SOC2/HIPAA language when vendor processes customer data; specify encryption-at-rest & in-transit for sensitive data.
- IP & Work Product: for custom development SOWs, ensure contractor assigns deliverables and grants necessary license to Redwood.
- Confidentiality: mutual NDA terms, carve-outs for pre-existing IP.
- Limitation of Liability: ensure caps are within procurement policy limits; escalate if vendor requests unlimited liability.
- Subcontracting & audit rights: include vendor obligation to notify subcontracting and Redwood audit rights for critical vendors.

7) Exceptions, change orders, and renewals
- Exception process: any deviation from standard playbook requires a documented exception form, approval chain, and acceptance by Legal and Finance.
- Change orders: must reference original contract ID, list delta of scope/price/dates, and be approved using same authority levels as original agreement.
- Renewals: procurement to create renewal checklist 90/60/30 days before term end, re-assess vendor performance and RevRec implications (auto-renewal clauses flagged for notice periods).

8) Roles, ownership, and SLAs
- Procurement: owner of supplier onboarding, PO issuance, tracking approvals (SLA: 3 business days for standard PR validation).
- Legal: owner of clause negotiation and final signoff (SLA: 5 business days for standard reviews; extended for escalations).
- Finance/RevRec: owner of recognition assessment and bookkeeping mapping (SLA: 3 business days after receiving redline).
- Billing/ERP: owner of vendor master maintenance and invoice processing (SLA: 5 business days post-executed docs).

9) Escalation matrix (summary)
- Contract value > $250K with high legal risk -> escalate to General Counsel and VP Finance.
- RevRec ambiguity that cannot be resolved in 5 business days -> escalate to Head of Finance for decision on revenue deferral or holdback policy.

10) Templates and artifacts (links)
- Standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) template (link to contract repo).
- Standard SOW template and acceptance language.
- Procurement PR template with required metadata fields.
- RevRec assessment form (fillable spreadsheet) to attach to PR.

Appendix A — Example scenario (illustrative):
- Situation: Annual SaaS commitment $300K, upfront annual prepay, includes implementation services and 12-month subscription.
- Actions: Procurement routes to manager + finance director. Legal confirms implementation SOW spells out deliverables. Finance flags significant financing component (upfront prepay) and requests amortization schedule; RevRec signoff documented. Billing updated to invoice upon contract signature and to amortize revenue monthly.

Appendix B — Change log:

If you need a walk-through session with Procurement + Finance to review how to complete the RevRec assessment form, contact procurement@redwood or finance-ops@redwood to schedule a 30-minute office hours slot.
